column3: Hello, I'm Arthur Ackerman.
YOU'LL HAVE TO SPEAK UP, DEAR!
I'm a little hard of hearing, you see.
Sorry, I'm Arthur Ackerman!
WHO'S THAT?
It's me! I'm an attorney at law!
YOU'RE A TERRIBLE BORE?
Are you doing this on purpose?
Hehe, who's to say?
Now, what is it you want?
Hello again.
What is it you want, Arthur?
Waasch schup?
Sorry old chap!
Can't understand a word!
Hello!
Ah, Ackerman, isn't it?
Arthur A. Ackerman, at your service.
I'm Kasper Bergmann, the treasurer of the Lady Unterwald estate.
Can you believe it, Arthur? What a messy state of affairs we've found ourselves in.
My feelings exactly.
Is there something I can help you with?
Hello again, Arthur.
How can I help you?
What do you make of this ledger, Bergmann?
Wh- Where did you get that!
I found it sealed away in the bottom of a locked drawer.
H- How peculiar! I've never seen that before in my life!
Really? Then we should pass this to the authorities when they arrive.
No!
I'd bet if they were to audit this ledger, the numbers wouldn't add up.
Listen, Arthur. I'm in a bit of a bind here.
Ashamed to say, I've fallen in with a rather unscrupulous individual.
Are you talking about Donny Donato?
I'm afraid so.
They managed to exploit my weakness, don't you see?
I'm a victim in all this, Arthur!
It's time to come clean. What's going on?
It's Donny. He's concocted a scheme to cheat at the casino tables.
We need to stop him, Arthur. I can't afford to lose more of the estate's money.
I can't understand you, sorry.
Did you find anything yet, Arthur?
We need to get that will back, Arthur.
Keep your guard up.
I'll monitor the situation from here.
We need to look into this further, Arthur.
Well, I've got Herman's keys.
Maybe we can look for evidence in his room?
The will is still missing.
Have you seen it anywhere, Arthur?
The missing will was here all along.
Better grab it before we lose it again, Arthur.
No, thanks!
What is this?
Not here.
I really don't want to touch that.
You hang on to it, Arthur.
Sorry, sir. The lounge and beyond are strictly off limits for now.
But there's a killer on the loose!
I'm the only one who had access to Lady Unterwald's will. I could be next!
No exceptions.
Sorry about Lady Unterwald.
What do you want, Arthur?
Hello there.
What's going on?
Ahh! Nothing!
Nobody has seen Herman since he vanished.
We're very concerned for his well-being!
Now, if you'll excuse us, we're going to check his room.
How's the breaking and entering going?
Not now, Arthur! We're trying to concentrate!
You're scaring me!
He's scaring me more!
Not thissh again.
How are you holding up, doc?
Doctor?
I think he's too distraught to talk right now.
I really thought Herman would be able to help us.
Forgive me, Lady Unterwald! I let you down.
I should have done something!
Pull yourself together!
There's nothing I could've done!
My god! Are you okay, Arthur?
How can I help, Arthur?
Good evening, sir.
Very good, sir.
The name's Ron.
I'm Arthur Ackerman!
Can I help you, Arthur?
I can't understand you, Arthur.
Arthur Ackerman, at your service.
Susanne Goldschmidt.
Do you need anything?
I heard about Lady Unterwald.
Not at the moment!
Until next time.
Lady Unterwald was murdered! What should I do?
Sorry to hear that, pal. If you suspect foul play, you could talk to the other passengers? Search around for clues, maybe?
I need another hint, what should I do!
Have you tried talking to everybody aboard the train? Searching Lady Unterwald's quarters might yield some results.
Head to Lady Unterwald's quarters, you might find some clues there!
Talk to the sleazy gentleman in the dining carriage, then follow his instructions.
I need to get into Lady Unterwald's room!
Looks like you'll have to get past the guard first. Can you distract them somehow?
I need another hint, how can I get past the guard?
Maybe you could convince them to leave their post. Do they have a weakness for anything?
The guard suffers from a fragrance allergy. Can you find something that would trigger it?
There's a sleazy gentleman in the dining carriage who may have what you need.
Get the perfumed note off the sleazy gentleman in the dining carriage. It should be potent enough to deal with the guard.
I've lost the will, how can I get it back?
Have you spotted it? The will might be flapping about somewhere.
I need another hint about the will.
Explore all the carriages, you might be able to grab it!
If you explore the carriages, you should be able to find it in the window!
I tried to get the will back, but it flew away!
There's a chance it flew by the sleeper carriage. Those rooms are locked though!
You'll have to gain access to passengers' quarters before you can get to the will.
You'll need to access Herman's quarters, too bad he lost his keys!
I found some keys, what should I do next?
Could you return those keys to their rightful owner?
I need another hint about the keys.
Those look like room keys. Can you locate the room number?
Those are Don's keys. Maybe find the right room and drop them off?
Where can I find Bergmann's ledger?
It sounds like Bergmann hid the ledger in a safe space.
I need another hint about the ledger.
The ledger is hidden in Lady Unterwald's quarters. But where?
Did you try looking in Lady Unterwald's desk drawer?
Lady Unterwald's drawer is locked, what do I do?
Perhaps you can find something to wedge it open?
I need another hint about the desk drawer.
I'll bet you could fit something thin and metal in between the gap.
If you wedged a metal hanger in there, I bet it'd open!
I found the ledger, what should I do with it?
You could use that ledger to apply some pressure, no doubt.
If Bergmann's been cooking the books, he wouldn't be too pleased to see that.
I'd confront Bergmann with it, let's see what he has to say for himself then!
How do I stop Don's scheme?
Have you observed Don at the roulette table? How is he manipulating the result?
I need another hint to stop Don's scheme!
Don's rigged the game with a magnetic ball. Can you disrupt the magnetic field?
A well-placed magnet of your own would likely throw off Don's scheme!
How do I stop Don getting more casino chips?
He must be getting them from somewhere! Is there a way to find out?
I need another hint to stop Don getting chips!
It looks like Don heads for his quarters, maybe you can beat him to it?
When Don leaves the table, get to his room before he does!
That's enough hints for now.
It's Doctor Hirsch's medical bag. I assume it's full of doctorly things.
April, are you there?
Diana?
What took you so long? I was starting to worry!
I have to go. I'll keep you updated.
Diana, abort! Abort the mission!
So, you finally made it.
I was beginning to doubt your abilities!
You didn't make it easy!
Were you talking to someone in here?
No. And that's none of your concern.
Well, what can you tell me?
Hm, you're right. A proper introduction is in order.
Diana Osterhagen, Inland Revenue Secret Service.
I'm a field operative, working under the British Government.
The Inland Revenue has a Secret Service branch? I've never heard of them.
That's the point, Arthur.
We've suspected the Unterwald estate has been concealing financial crimes for some time, but we weren't able to pin them down.
There was always an obstruction, someone with their thumb on the scale.
Not just a thumb, but maybe a hand.
We had nothing to go on, not until an informant made contact with the promise of information.
And...
You think I'm that informant?
The informant would be wearing a blue suit with a red rosette.
Are you suggesting that doesn't match your description?
The suit? Of course.
Lady Unterwald must have orchestrated this whole thing!
What's that?
Nothing! I was just thinking out loud.
So, what have you got? Do you have evidence of financial misconduct?
Herman's belongings are still here. It doesn't look like he fled.
Let's take a look around, maybe we'll find a clue.
I got it!
Well done, Arthur!
Where there's a will, there's a way!
Hellooo?
Is that you, detective?
Hey, you're not Herman!
What are you doing here?
We were just...
We could ask you the same question.
We were looking for the detective.
Wait, what's that you're holding?
This is just a piece of paper, all very inconsequential.
You found the missing will?
We can do the reading now, Mr Ackerman!
I don't think that's a good idea.
We should get started right away!
There's still a lot of cross-referencing we need to per-
Oh, we insist!
What drives a man to own this many bow ties?
Your guess is as good as mine. But we're not here to pursue crimes of fashion.
Still mighty suspicious, if you ask me.
It's a cheap WHISPERNOTE knock-off.
No self-respecting writer should be opting for an off-brand model.
Are you comparing office supplies right now?
‘Herman Merman And The Suburban Burden'
Not one of his better titles. These must be unfinished works.
I can't say I've read any of these before, and I don't think I'll be starting now.
Looks like those twins were rifling through Herman's belongings.
Ugh. They give me the heebie-jeebies.
It's a small collection of Dirk Chiselton adventures.
The paperbacks are dog-eared, like he read them in a bad mood.
And thasch why...
...youUu' my besschd fierend!
Yes, Arthur.
We're all very pleased that you're finally having a good time.
But I can't understand a word you're saying.
None of us can!
Oof, that coffee did the trick, but my head is killing me.
I hope I didn't embarrass myself.
Well, Arthur?
What does it say?
I'm not sure I should--
GET ON WITH IT!
Alright, alright!
It reads as follows...
I, Lady Unterwald, being of sound mind and legal capacity...
Leave my entire estate to...
You poisonous goat!
You turned her against us.
I -
We were right to distrust you!
Hand over that will!
Hey, that's your hearing horn!
It's all starting to make sense now.
What is it, mother?
Arthur clearly manipulated my dear sister's living will in his own favour.
Then murdered her to claim the estate for himself!
It's not what it looks like!
Oh dear.
Seize him!
I should confront Bergmann about this ledger.
Everything has been packed away, I must have missed their opening hours.
When this is all over, I'd like to curl up in this reading nook.
Nah. I think enough people have died on stage tonight.
It looks expensive, and it smells like mahogany!
This led to the backstage area before they locked it up.
I suppose it's a potential crime scene now.
It's the guest list for the Green Room. VIPs only.
I don't recognise most of these names, but I see Herman made the cut!
Hmm.
I guess nobody's there.
Helloo?
Looks like nobody's home.
Anyone in?
They must have left.
I guess nobody's home.
I really shhould sober upp first.
The luggage room.
It's room 302.
It's room 304.
It's room 305.
It's room 306.
The door sign reads ''DO NOT DISTURB!''
It's a fancy cart for transporting luggage.
I've only ever seen these in hotels!
I think this was Lady Unterwald's husband.
I wonder what happened to him?
''George Unterwald.''
''A loving husband. Gone, but not forgotten.''
''Lady J. Unterwald.''
''Heiress Of the Unterwald Empire.''
Misplaced?
Must I remind you of who I am?
Herman Merman and the Murmuring German?
Herman Merman and the Squirmin' Chairman?
Sorry sir, not a big reader.
Not even ''Herman Merman and the Sermon of Vermin'' ?
No, sir...
My point being, I don't misplace things. I solve cases!
That's excellent news, sir.
I'm sure you'll have no problem with the case of the missing room keys.
Well...
Yes, you're quite right!
Mr Masson thought I might find the medical briefcase in here.
Hey, that cheese I left has gone!
Good thing I've got some more with me.
That solves where Herman's keys went.
Hm. It looks like a rodent has eaten their way through this section.
It looks too heavy to move.
This could be the medical briefcase I'm looking for!
They're all tightly secured to the luggage rack.
I wonder what's inside?
Locked tight. I don't think I'm getting through there.
Bergmann said that he'd hidden the company accounts ledger somewhere in here.
Who'd want to kill Lady Unterwald?
Ah, Arthur. Thank you for coming.
Doctor Hirsch, at your service. I'm Lady Unterwald's personal physician.
Or, at least, I was.
I'm sorry about Lady Unterwald, Doctor Hearse.
It's Hirsch. H-I-R-S-C-H!
Ohh, they're not going to call me Doctor Hearse, are they?
I can see the headlines already. The doctor of death, who failed to save Lady Unterwald!
There's nothing I could've done without my medical briefcase!
How can I help? What do you need?
With Herman gone, I need you to help me find some answers.
Answers?
Help me look around, does anything look out of place?
This is the ledger that Bergmann mentioned.
I should ask him about those discrepancies.
I think that did it!
Stand back, Arthur!
What is all this paperwork?
This is one of Lady Unterwald's wills, alright.
Another will?
Wait, there's another one!
And another!
There are hundreds of wills here.
Every alteration Lady Unterwald ever made. These could go back years!
Somebody would have to go through all this paperwork to check.
My goodness!
Finally, some bureaucracy!
So, did you find what you were looking for?
Not exactly.
I'll still need to locate the lost will, but I should be able to compare it against these revisions.
How's the espionage going?
The safe didn't contain any financial records, if that's why you're here.
No, that's not the reason I came.
Listen, I recorded a suspicious phone call shortly after the death of Lady Unterwald.
What kind of phone call?
Here, you can play it on your recorder.
I should attend to Lady Unterwald before I leave.
I can't leave, Doctor Hirsch still needs my help.
I'll need to figure out how to get that will back.
I'm afraid we must all come to live with our mistakes, Arthur.
I never took Lady Unterwald to be particularly musical.
I don't think it was a secret that she disdained most noises.
She didn't. At least not to my knowledge.
Lady Unterwald was clearly respected and admired.
So who'd want to take her out of the picture?
I hope we'll be able to find out, Arthur.
It's a habanero pepper plant. Stay well away if you want to keep your taste buds.
Lady Unterwald hated balloons.
Who's there?
Nobody!
We can only hope these coats were made from faux fur.
Lady Unterwald hated all that clacking.
Jian Liu? You know, I haven't seen him for a while.
It seems to be stuck.
Arthur, please leave that alone.
Didn't anyone ever tell you it's rude to go through a lady's drawers?
Sorry.
Arthur, stop that now!
It won't happen again.
Arthur, if you want to keep your fingers you'll leave that drawer alone.
I can't help myself!
I better not.
The drawer is stuck.
If I wedged something in the gap, I might be able to pry it open.
Bergmann could've put that ledger in this drawer.
It's an empty drawer.
